materials.name: Healer's Moss
materials.desc: Springy green moss that smells of wet stone and mint; pressed into wounds it staunches bleeding. The staple of every healing potion.

materials.name: Silverleaf
materials.desc: Narrow leaves with a silvery underside that shimmer in the breeze. Steeped, they soothe fevers and knit shallow cuts.

materials.name: Yarrow Sprig
materials.desc: Flat white flower heads with a sharp, camphor smell. Soldiers chew it to slow bleeding; alchemists use it as a cheap filler.

materials.name: Willow Bark
materials.desc: Bitter strips of grey bark that dull aches when chewed. A humble painkiller and a common potion thinner.

materials.name: Mendwort
materials.desc: Fleshy, ribbed leaves that ooze a clear gel which seals cuts as you watch. The backbone of greater healing draughts.

materials.name: Stone Milk
materials.desc: A soft white paste that seeps from cave walls, cool and chalky to the touch. Dwarven healers pack it on broken bones.

materials.name: Kingsbalm Lily
materials.desc: A golden trumpet-shaped lily whose scent alone makes the weary stand straighter. Its nectar anchors superior healing elixirs.

materials.name: Sunmend Orchid
materials.desc: A pale orchid that only opens when sunlight strikes it, glowing faintly afterwards. Mends torn muscle and cracked bone in minutes.

materials.name: Everbloom Heartroot
materials.desc: A pulsing, red-veined root that regrows if even a sliver remains in the soil. Healers use it to restore lost fingers and limbs.

materials.name: Knotwood Bracket
materials.desc: A lumpy shelf fungus that regrows overnight when broken off. Distilled, it lends potions a stubborn regenerative quality.

materials.name: Cleansing Sage
materials.desc: Woolly grey-green leaves with a smoky, resinous smell. Burned or brewed, it draws toxins from the blood; the core of antitoxin.

materials.name: Wyrmbane Thistle
materials.desc: A spiny purple thistle whose sap tastes like copper. Legend says it grows where dragons were slain; it neutralises strong venoms.

materials.name: Purity Lotus
materials.desc: A snow-white lotus floating on still, holy waters. A single petal purges disease and poison from a body entirely.

materials.name: Feverfew
materials.desc: Tiny daisy-like flowers with a bitter bite. Brewed as a tea to fight fevers and camp sickness.

materials.name: Wild Garlic
materials.desc: Pungent white bulbs with broad leaves. Cooks love it; folk hang it against vampires with mixed success.

materials.name: Bellshade
materials.desc: A drooping purple bell-flower that gives way to glossy black berries. Nightshade's cousin: a few berries sedate, a handful kills.

materials.name: Drowsy Poppy
materials.desc: A crimson poppy whose milky sap smells of honey and dust. Its dried seed-heads are ground into sleeping draughts.

materials.name: Slumberlily
materials.desc: A heavy-headed blue lily that exhales a drowsy perfume at night. Its pollen is the key to potent sleep poisons and dust.

materials.name: Widow's Hood
materials.desc: A black-capped mushroom with a hood of lacy gills. Its spores numb the tongue first, then the limbs — assassins favour it.

materials.name: Deathcap Toadstool
materials.desc: An innocent-looking olive toadstool with a faint sweet smell. Nearly every part is lethal; poisoners reduce it to a tasteless powder.

materials.name: Black Lotus
materials.desc: An ink-black lotus that drinks light around it. Its resin is among the deadliest poisons known and outlawed in most cities.

materials.name: Stiffweed
materials.desc: A rigid, grey-stemmed weed that stings like nettle and leaves skin numb for hours. Used in paralytic poisons and numbing salves.

materials.name: Dread Nettle
materials.desc: Dark-veined nettles whose sting triggers a cold, unreasoning panic. Brewed into fear-poisons and terror incense.

materials.name: Ravings Cap
materials.desc: A spiralled violet mushroom that whispers when it dries. Eating it brings visions — and sometimes madness.

materials.name: Rotbloom
materials.desc: A fleshy brown flower that stinks of carrion to draw flies. Its sticky pollen carries wasting sickness; plague-doctors study it.

materials.name: Water Hemlock
materials.desc: Innocent white umbrella flowers above a deadly, parsnip-like root. A classic poisoner's staple.

materials.name: Oxheart Tuber
materials.desc: A heavy, dark-red tuber the size of a fist, earthy and sweet. Farmers eat it for stamina; potion-makers for endurance tonics.

materials.name: Giant's Knuckle Root
materials.desc: A gnarled, stone-hard root shaped like a clenched fist. Boiled down, it gives draughts of bull-like strength.

materials.name: Stoneroot
materials.desc: A root so dense it rings like rock when tapped, and grows straight through granite. Lends potions a skin-hardening quality.

materials.name: Quickthorn Berry
materials.desc: Tiny, tart orange berries on a jittery bush that twitches in the wind. They quicken the heart and the reflexes.

materials.name: Wakeberry
materials.desc: Small red berries whose bitter seeds banish drowsiness. Guards chew them through long night watches.

materials.name: Clingvine
materials.desc: A tough, hairy ivy whose tendrils grip stone like tiny hands. Braided into ropes and climbing gloves.

materials.name: Spidergrip Moss
materials.desc: A velvety black moss that sticks to anything it touches, including fingers. The secret ingredient of spider-climbing elixirs.

materials.name: Gillweed Kelp
materials.desc: Ribbon-like green kelp with feathery frills that pulse in the current. Chewed or brewed, it lets the lungs take air from water.

materials.name: Bladderwrack
materials.desc: Brown seaweed studded with air-filled pods that pop underfoot. Rich in salts; a cheap base for water-themed draughts.

materials.name: Sea Lettuce
materials.desc: Bright green, paper-thin seaweed that tastes of the tide. Coastal folk eat it raw.

materials.name: Abyssal Driftkelp
materials.desc: A deep-blue kelp that grows in the sunless trenches, cold as snow to the touch. It lets divers endure crushing depths.

materials.name: Ghostpetal
materials.desc: A flower with petals as clear as glass; you can only find it by its faint scent of rain. The heart of invisibility potions.

materials.name: Glasswing Orchid
materials.desc: An orchid so transparent that only its shadow gives it away — and sometimes not even that. Used for lasting invisibility magic.

materials.name: Mirage Lotus
materials.desc: A shimmering desert lotus that appears to be several flowers at once. Illusionists grind it into their dusts and inks.

materials.name: Mistcap
materials.desc: A small grey mushroom that puffs out a sheet of pale fog when squeezed. Used for smoke pellets and minor illusions.

materials.name: Wind Seed
materials.desc: A downy seed-puff that rises rather than falls, tugging at your fingers. Bundles of them go into potions of flying and levitation.

materials.name: Skyfloat Thistle
materials.desc: A silver thistle-head that drifts upward and refuses to land. Used in carpets, brooms and flight magic of real strength.

materials.name: Featherfall Fern
materials.desc: Delicate fronds that flutter down slower than a leaf should. Alchemists use them to soften falls.

materials.name: Emberbloom
materials.desc: A crimson flower with petals that glow like coals and are warm to the touch. Brewed into fire-resistance potions.

materials.name: Ashlily
materials.desc: A grey lily that sprouts in freshly burned ground and smells faintly of smoke. Used for fire-starting salves and minor fire wards.

materials.name: Frost Lichen
materials.desc: Blue-white lichen that crackles like frost and never thaws. Distilled, it grants resistance to biting cold.

materials.name: Snowcap Berry
materials.desc: Pale blue berries with a crust of rime; they taste of mint and winter. Eaten, they warm the body against cold.

materials.name: Icebloom Saxifrage
materials.desc: A star-shaped white flower that grows from cracks in glacier ice. Its petals stay frozen solid; used in frost weapons and oils.

materials.name: Lionsmane Thistle
materials.desc: A tawny, shaggy-headed thistle that stands tall even in gales. Its tea steadies nerves; it is the core of heroism draughts.

materials.name: Mindbloom Orchid
materials.desc: A pink-and-grey orchid folded like a brain, humming faintly when people speak near it. The key to mind-reading elixirs.

materials.name: Seer's Leaf
materials.desc: A broad leaf with an eye-shaped pattern that seems to follow you. Chewed, it brings visions of far places.

materials.name: Eyebright
materials.desc: A small white flower with a yellow eye. Eyewash made from it sharpens sight; diviners use it in scrying mixes.

materials.name: Veilpierce Eyebright
materials.desc: A violet eyebright variety that only grows where the veil between worlds is thin. Eyedrops made from it see through illusion.

materials.name: Ageless Lotus
materials.desc: A blue lotus that never wilts; legend says it has bloomed for centuries. Elixirs made from it slow or reverse aging.

materials.name: Rememberwort
materials.desc: A pale, velvet moss that smells like old books. Brewed, it sharpens recall; scholars sip it before exams.

materials.name: Four-Leaf Clover
materials.desc: A rare four-lobed clover leaf, pressed and dried. Cheap charms and luck potions need at least one.

materials.name: Lover's Rose
materials.desc: A velvet-red rose whose scent makes people linger and smile. Perfumers and enchanters build charm magic around it.

materials.name: Giantcap Mushroom
materials.desc: A mushroom that doubles in size every night until it is picked. Essential for enlargement potions.

materials.name: Shrinking Violet
materials.desc: A tiny violet that folds shut and shrinks when touched. The core ingredient of diminution draughts.

materials.name: Hushmoss
materials.desc: A thick, deep-green moss that swallows sound; footfalls on it make no noise. Lines the boots of thieves.

materials.name: Whisperleaf Vine
materials.desc: A slender grey-green vine whose leaves rustle in perfect silence and shift colour to match their surroundings. Woven into elven cloaks and boots.

materials.name: Nullthorn
materials.desc: A dull grey bramble on which spells fizzle and die. Mages hate it; spell-breakers and wardens prize it.

materials.name: Sourbog Pitcher
materials.desc: A pitcher plant whose cup brims with digestive acid strong enough to dissolve beetles. Harvested for acid flasks.

materials.name: Stormbloom
materials.desc: A spiky blue flower that crackles with static and only opens after a thunderstorm. Used in lightning oils and storm magic.

materials.name: Wailing Puffball
materials.desc: A round white puffball that shrieks when burst. Used in thunderstones and alarm charms.

materials.name: Gloomsight Fungus
materials.desc: A tiny black mushroom with a glossy cap like a cat's eye. Chewed, it lets the eye gather the faintest light.

materials.name: Glowcap
materials.desc: A pale blue mushroom that glows softly in the dark. Crushed into paints and lamps that need no flame.

materials.name: Dreamcap
materials.desc: A thin-stalked mushroom with a golden cap that brings vivid dreams. Seers use it; the unwary lose a night.

materials.name: Cave Truffle
materials.desc: A knobbly black truffle with an intense, earthy smell. Delicious; also a hearty trail food.

materials.name: Tomb Mold
materials.desc: A grey-green fuzz that blooms on old coffins and smells of damp cloth. Necromancers use it in wasting curses.

materials.name: Hag's Fingers
materials.desc: Long, knuckled grey mushrooms that grow in clusters like reaching fingers. Witches use them for hexes.

materials.name: Gutter Cap
materials.desc: A slimy brown mushroom from damp alleys and sewers. Rat-catchers use it for bait and poison.

materials.name: Heather
materials.desc: Tough little purple flowers that carpet hillsides. Used in brewing and for bedding.

materials.name: Sweetgrass
materials.desc: A long grass that smells of vanilla when dried. Braided and burned in blessing rites.

materials.name: Chamomile
materials.desc: Small daisy flowers with an apple scent. A calming tea and a mild sleep aid.

materials.name: Flax Stalks
materials.desc: Pale stalks retted and combed into fibre for linen and bowstrings.

materials.name: Trailberries
materials.desc: Mixed wild berries — bramble, bilberry and haw. Good trail food and a cheap dye.

materials.name: Wild Honeycomb
materials.desc: A dripping slab of wild honey and wax. Mead-makers and healers both value it.

materials.name: Samphire
materials.desc: Salty, crunchy green shoots from tidal flats. A sailor's cure for scurvy.

materials.name: Marshmallow Root
materials.desc: A sticky, pale root from marsh edges. Soothes coughs and sore throats.

materials.name: Cattail Root
materials.desc: Starchy roots from reed beds. Survival food; the fluffy heads make tinder.

materials.name: Aloe Leaf
materials.desc: A thick spined leaf full of cool gel. Soothes burns and sunburn.

materials.name: Oak Gall
materials.desc: A hard woody ball formed on oak twigs. Crushed with iron salts it makes permanent black ink.

materials.name: Woad Leaf
materials.desc: Greenish leaves that ferment into a deep blue dye. Used by painters and warriors alike.

materials.name: Mandrake Root
materials.desc: A forked, man-shaped root that shrieks when pulled from the ground. Used in sleep and fear magic.

materials.name: Wolfsbane
materials.desc: A tall, hooded blue flower that is poisonous to handle. Rubbed on blades, it wards against lycanthropes.

materials.name: Belladonna
materials.desc: Shiny black berries and dull purple bells. A few drops widen the pupils; more stop the heart.

materials.name: Bloodmoss
materials.desc: A dark red moss that feeds on spilled blood where battles were fought. Used in blood magic and vampiric cures alike.

materials.name: Bog Myrtle
materials.desc: A sweet-smelling bog shrub that repels midges. Brewers once used it instead of hops.

materials.name: Yew Stave
materials.desc: A springy stave of yew with golden heartwood and pale sapwood. The finest bow wood in the world; its needles are poisonous.

materials.name: Rowan Wood
materials.desc: Smooth grey wood from the mountain ash, with red berries. Fey and witches shun it; charms and wards are carved from it.

materials.name: Elder Wood
materials.desc: Hollow-pithed elder branches, light and fragrant. Traditional wood for wands and pipes.

materials.name: Blackthorn Wood
materials.desc: Dark, thorny wood that twists as it grows. Used for walking sticks, cudgels and curse-wands.

materials.name: Ironwood
materials.desc: A dense, dark-brown wood that sinks in water and turns axe blades. Makes shields and hafts as hard as steel.

materials.name: Darkwood
materials.desc: A charcoal-grey timber as light as balsa but as strong as oak. Prized for light shields, bows and armour.

materials.name: Ancient Oak Heartwood
materials.desc: Dense, amber-ringed heartwood from an oak older than kingdoms, still warm as if alive. The finest core for druidic staves.

materials.name: Fey-Touched Wood
materials.desc: Pale wood with shifting, silvery grain that sprouts leaves in moonlight. Makes wands and instruments with a fey lilt.

materials.name: Gloomwood
materials.desc: Black, cold wood that seems to absorb light and never casts a proper shadow. Used for assassins' bows and shadow staves.

materials.name: Petrified Wood
materials.desc: Ancient wood turned to banded stone, every ring preserved. Used in petrification magic and stone-skin wards.

materials.name: Lightning-Struck Wood
materials.desc: Split, blackened timber from a tree hit by lightning; it still makes your hair stand up. Used for storm wands and staves.

materials.name: Driftwood
materials.desc: Silver-grey wood smoothed by years in the sea. Sailors carve charms from it.

materials.name: Bog Oak
materials.desc: Oak preserved for millennia in peat, black as jet and hard as iron. Carved into grim relics and sturdy clubs.

materials.name: Moonwillow Branch
materials.desc: A silvery willow branch that glows under the moon and weeps sweet dew. Used for fey staves and illusion wands.

materials.name: Golden Bough
materials.desc: A branch with bark like beaten gold and leaves that chime. Only grows on the Upper Planes; staffs of power are carved from it.

materials.name: Birch Bark
materials.desc: Papery white bark that burns even when wet. Tinder, canoe-skins and writing strips.

materials.name: Silver Birch Bark
materials.desc: Bark from birches that grow in moonlit glades, shining like polished silver. Used in wards against undead.

materials.name: Ironbark
materials.desc: Thick, grooved bark as hard as iron plates. Ground into barkskin salves and used in armour.

materials.name: Mangrove Bark
materials.desc: Red-brown bark from salt-loving mangroves. Rich in tannin for tanning hides.

materials.name: Pine Resin
materials.desc: Sticky, amber-coloured pitch. Seals, torches and glues.

materials.name: Dragon's Blood Resin
materials.desc: Dark red resin from the umbrella-shaped dragon tree, smelling of spice. Used in fire incense and strength tonics.

materials.name: Frankincense
materials.desc: Milky golden tears of resin from a desert tree, heady when burned. Temples use it in consecration and blessing rites.

materials.name: Myrrh
materials.desc: Reddish, bitter resin used to anoint the dead and heal wounds. Embalmers and healers both keep it.

materials.name: Bloodwood Sap
materials.desc: Crimson sap that bleeds from cuts in the bloodwood tree and clots like blood. Used in healing and blood-binding rites.

materials.name: Amberpine Sap
materials.desc: A golden, very sticky sap that sets hard in hours. Alchemists use it to bind reagents together.

materials.name: Quartz Crystal
materials.desc: A clear, six-sided crystal point. A cheap spellcasting focus that amplifies whatever is channelled through it.

materials.name: Rose Quartz
materials.desc: Soft pink quartz, warm and cloudy. Love charms and calming amulets.

materials.name: Smoky Quartz
materials.desc: Brown-black, translucent quartz that dims light passing through it. Wards and shadow charms.

materials.name: Mica Sheets
materials.desc: Flaky, glittering sheets of mineral that peel apart like pages. Lantern panes and spell components.

materials.name: Amber
materials.desc: Honey-gold fossil resin that sometimes holds an ancient insect. Warm to the touch; used in time and preservation magic.

materials.name: Jet
materials.desc: Deep black fossilised wood polished to a glassy sheen, surprisingly light. Mourning jewellery and wards against the dead.

materials.name: Obsidian
materials.desc: Glossy black volcanic glass that fractures into razor edges. Arrowheads, dagger blades and scrying mirrors.

materials.name: Garnet
materials.desc: A deep red stone like a pomegranate seed. A travellers' charm; used in fire and blood magic.

materials.name: Amethyst
materials.desc: Purple quartz said to keep the mind clear. Used against charm and intoxication.

materials.name: Lapis Lazuli
materials.desc: Deep blue stone with gold flecks like a night sky. Ground into ultramarine paint and knowledge charms.

materials.name: Malachite
materials.desc: Banded green stone like a slice of agate. Ground as pigment and carved into earth amulets.

materials.name: Turquoise
materials.desc: Sky-blue stone with brown veins. A riders' charm against falls and ill winds.

materials.name: Moonstone
materials.desc: A milky stone with a blue sheen that shifts like moonlight on water. Lunar, fey and light magic.

materials.name: Bloodstone
materials.desc: Dark green stone speckled with red like drops of blood. Healers carry it; used in regeneration rings.

materials.name: Onyx
materials.desc: Black-and-white banded stone, cold and heavy. Necromancers use it as the focus for animating the dead.

materials.name: Jade
materials.desc: Cool green stone that rings when struck. Carved into protective talismans and armour charms.

materials.name: Opal
materials.desc: A milky stone flickering with every colour as it turns. Illusion and glamour magic.

materials.name: Topaz
materials.desc: A golden-yellow gem that holds a static charge after rubbing and snaps at fingertips. Lightning magic.

materials.name: Aquamarine
materials.desc: A sea-green-blue gem as clear as shallow water. Sailors' charm and water-breathing foci.

materials.name: Peridot
materials.desc: An olive-green gem found in volcanic rock, warm and bright. Growth and plant magic.

materials.name: Sunstone
materials.desc: An orange gem with glittering inclusions that glow in daylight. Radiant and light magic.

materials.name: Fire Opal
materials.desc: A translucent orange opal with flames that seem to dance inside it. A rare fire focus for wands and flame-tongued blades.

materials.name: Ruby
materials.desc: A blood-red gem that glows faintly from within when held to firelight. The finest focus for fire magic.

materials.name: Sapphire
materials.desc: A deep blue gem, cold to the touch even in the sun. Frost weapons and arcane foci.

materials.name: Emerald
materials.desc: A green gem that seems to hold a forest's depth. Nature, growth and divination magic.

materials.name: Raw Diamond
materials.desc: A rough, greasy-looking stone that blazes when cut. The ultimate ward and resurrection focus; grind it to make diamond dust.

materials.name: Star Ruby
materials.desc: A ruby with a six-rayed star that shifts as it turns. Very powerful fire magic and luck charms.

materials.name: Star Sapphire
materials.desc: A deep blue sapphire with a silver star that glints like a distant sun. Arcane and cold magic of the highest order.

materials.name: Black Opal
materials.desc: A black opal flashing green and blue fire from its depths. Shadow and illusion magic of great power.

materials.name: Black Pearl
materials.desc: A dark, lustrous pearl from deep oyster beds, heavy and cold. Necromancy and water magic.

materials.name: Red Coral
materials.desc: Branching, blood-red coral, hard and smooth when polished. Talismans against drowning and water charms.

materials.name: Black Coral
materials.desc: Glossy black coral from deep reefs, bending like horn when warmed. Water and death magic.

materials.name: Lodestone
materials.desc: A heavy grey stone that tugs iron filings toward it and always swings north. Compasses, finding charms and magnetic rings.

materials.name: Glowcrystal
materials.desc: A pale blue crystal that sheds soft, sourceless light in darkness. Everburning lamps and light charms.

materials.name: Resonant Crystal
materials.desc: A tall crystal that rings when struck and repeats sounds made near it. Used in sound and thunder magic.

materials.name: Prism Crystal
materials.desc: A clear crystal that splits light into dancing rainbows. Illusion and light magic.

materials.name: Arcane Crystal
materials.desc: A violet crystal that hums with raw magic and warms near spellcasters. The heart of staffs and wands.

materials.name: Echo Geode
materials.desc: A plain, rounded stone with sparkling crystals inside that whisper back your words hours later. Sound and messenger charms.

materials.name: Rime Crystal
materials.desc: A hexagonal crystal of frozen air that never melts and fogs your breath. Frost wands and winter charms.

materials.name: Aurora Glass
materials.desc: A thin sheet of shimmering glass formed where the aurora touches the ice, rippling green and violet. Light and cold magic.

materials.name: Rock Salt
materials.desc: Coarse pink-grey salt dug from dry lakebeds and mines. Preserving meat and pouring warding circles.

materials.name: Sea Salt
materials.desc: Flaky white salt raked from tidal pans. Cooking, preserving and warding against spirits.

materials.name: Natron
materials.desc: A dry, soapy salt from desert lakes that draws water from anything. Embalmers use it to preserve corpses; necromancers to prepare them.

materials.name: Alum
materials.desc: Astringent white crystals that pucker the tongue. Tanning, dye-fixing and styptic pencils.

materials.name: Raw Chalk
materials.desc: Soft white limestone that crumbles to powder. Drawing summoning circles and marking trails.

materials.name: Flint
materials.desc: A glassy grey nodule that sparks against steel. Fire-starting and knapped blades.

materials.name: Potter's Clay
materials.desc: Smooth, grey riverbank clay, cool and slick. Pots, moulds and golem bodies.

materials.name: Marble
materials.desc: White, blue-veined stone that takes a high polish. Statues, altars and fine building.

materials.name: Cinnabar
materials.desc: A blood-red ore that sweats quicksilver when heated. Dangerous; used for vermilion and quicksilver.

materials.name: Orpiment
materials.desc: A brilliant golden-yellow mineral, beautiful and poisonous. Pigment and rat poison.

materials.name: Verdigris
materials.desc: A green crust scraped from old copper and bronze. Pigment and acid reagent.

materials.name: Chimney Soot
materials.desc: Fine black soot scraped from flues. Ink and paint.

materials.name: Glass Sand
materials.desc: Pale, very fine sand that melts clear. The raw stuff of vials and lenses.

materials.name: Volcanic Black Sand
materials.desc: Glittering black sand from volcanic beaches, warm underfoot. Fire glass and hourglasses.

materials.name: Sunsand
materials.desc: Golden sand that stays hot long after sunset and glows faintly at night. Used in radiant glass and light magic.

materials.name: Fulgurite
materials.desc: A hollow glass tube formed where lightning struck sand. Used in lightning wands.

materials.name: Desert Rose
materials.desc: Rosette-shaped gypsum crystals grown in desert sand like stone petals. Charms and earth magic.

materials.name: Selenite
materials.desc: A clear, silky crystal that glows faintly under moonlight. Moon charms and light magic.

materials.name: Glacier Blue Ice
materials.desc: Dense, ancient ice that is almost sapphire blue and keeps its chill for days. Cold packs, frost oils and cooling potions.

materials.name: Meteoric Iron
materials.desc: A pitted, dark metal fallen from the sky, still faintly warm. Holds enchantments like no earthly iron and bites through magical wards.

materials.name: Sea Glass
materials.desc: Frosted, rounded shards of glass polished by the waves. Cheap charms and decorative inlay.

materials.name: Ambergris
materials.desc: A waxy grey lump washed ashore, smelling of sea and musk. Perfumers and charm-makers pay well for it.

materials.name: Conch Shell
materials.desc: A spiralled pink shell that holds the roar of the sea. Horns, signal trumpets and sound magic.

materials.name: Nautilus Shell
materials.desc: A perfectly spiralled, chambered shell, mathematically precise. Time magic and depth charms.

materials.name: Grave Lily
materials.desc: A waxy white lily that grows only on graves, smelling faintly of cold earth. Used in necromancy and funeral rites.

materials.name: Arcane Residue
materials.desc: Glittering, faintly humming dust scraped from where old spells burned into stone. Powders for scrolls and wands.

materials.name: Runestone Fragment
materials.desc: A broken chunk of carved stone whose runes still glimmer. Ground into inks or set into foci.

materials.name: Deepglow Lichen
materials.desc: A violet lichen that glows where wild magic seeps from Underdark rock. Used in light and arcane magic.

materials.name: Umbral Crystal
materials.desc: A black crystal that makes light around it dim; peer through it and darkness becomes clear. Shadow and darkvision magic.

materials.name: Moonpetal
materials.desc: A pale, luminous flower that opens only under moonlight and glows like a small moon; it withers into grey dust if picked in daylight. Used in fey, moonlight and light magic.

materials.name: Glamour Pollen
materials.desc: Shimmering golden pollen from Feywild blossoms; one breath and everything looks lovelier. Charm dusts, glamour oils and illusion magic.

materials.name: Dreamfruit
materials.desc: A dusky violet fruit that tastes different to everyone who bites it. Eaten, it brings prophetic dreams; distilled, it anchors sleep and dream magic.

materials.name: Fey Clover
materials.desc: A golden, five-leafed clover whose leaves curl towards whoever is nearest. Stronger than any mortal clover for luck charms and potions.

materials.name: Faerie Ring Mushroom
materials.desc: A pale mushroom picked from a perfect faerie ring, still humming with the ring's power. Teleportation and fey-crossing magic.

materials.name: Starlit Dew
materials.desc: Dew gathered from Feywild grass at dawn, sparkling with trapped starlight; it evaporates within the hour. Delicate restorative and healing magic.

materials.name: Wishbloom
materials.desc: A single silver-and-gold flower that blooms once a century in the heart of the Feywild. Legends say its nectar can bend fate itself.

materials.name: Gloom Moss
materials.desc: A grey-black moss that drinks in light and muffles footsteps; a patch of it looks like a hole in the world. Lines shadow cloaks and quiets boots.

materials.name: Soulless Ash
materials.desc: Cold, weightless grey ash from Shadowfell pyres that burned without flame or warmth. It leaves fingertips numb; necromancers use it to hollow out and bind the dead.

materials.name: Shadowsilk Thistle
materials.desc: A black thistle whose seed-floss can be spun into silk that bends light around it. Invisibility and shadow magic.

materials.name: Sorrowbloom
materials.desc: A drooping, colourless flower that radiates a quiet, crushing despair; people who sleep near it do not want to wake. Used in fear, despair and calming magic.

materials.name: Mourning Salt
materials.desc: Grey, bitter salt crystallised along the shores of a Shadowfell lake said to be made of tears. Sprinkled in grave wards and curses of grief.

materials.name: Dusk Pearl
materials.desc: A smoke-grey pearl with a black core that visibly swallows lamplight. Found only in the lightless waters of the Shadowfell; a very-rare keystone for shadow and undeath magic.

materials.name: Living Flame Ember
materials.desc: An ember that flickers with its own will and burns without fuel. The core of powerful fire magic; it gutters out within an hour unless sealed in a crystal phial or iron brazier.

materials.name: Cinder Salt
materials.desc: Red, crackling salt crystals that pop and spark when wet, scraped from the ash-flats of Elemental Fire. A common fire reagent for alchemist's fire and fire oils.

materials.name: Magma Glass
materials.desc: Heavy, dark glass shot through with red veins that still glow, from the crust of cooled magma rivers. Blades and arrowheads that burn on contact.

materials.name: Eternal Coal
materials.desc: A black coal with a heart of orange light that burns for years without being consumed. Forges fed with it reach adamantine-melting heat.

materials.name: Primordial Flame
materials.desc: A tiny seed of the first fire, white-gold and impossibly bright, that must be caught in a vessel within a minute or it returns to the plane. A legendary keystone for supreme fire magic.

materials.name: Pure Water Pearl
materials.desc: A flawless pearl of solidified water, perfectly clear, that stays cool and damp in the hand. A rare keystone for water breathing, water walking and tide magic.

materials.name: Primordial Brine
materials.desc: Thick, deep-blue brine from the Plane of Water, heavy with ancient salts and faintly luminous. A strong reagent for water and swimming potions.

materials.name: Eternal Ice
materials.desc: Pale blue ice from the frozen frontier where Elemental Water meets Air, which no fire can melt. A very-rare keystone for cold, frost weapons and freezing magic.

materials.name: Tideheart Pearl
materials.desc: A pearl the size of a fist that swells and shrinks with a slow tidal pulse, taken from the deepest reach of the Plane of Water. A legendary keystone for mastery over water and storms.

materials.name: Currentweave Kelp
materials.desc: Silver-green kelp whose ribbons always stream against the current, native to the Plane of Water but also rooted wherever elemental springs well up on mortal seabeds. Brewed into swimming and speed draughts.

materials.name: Stormglass
materials.desc: A marble-sized glass bead with a tiny, living storm raging inside; lightning flickers and it crackles against the ear. A rare keystone for lightning and storm magic.

materials.name: Solid Cloud
materials.desc: A tuft of cloud from Elemental Air that has grown firm enough to hold, cool and faintly damp. Woven into levitation cushions and flight charms.

materials.name: Earthmote Stone
materials.desc: A chunk of rock that floats in mid-air and gently resists being pushed down. Used in levitation magic and flying constructs.

materials.name: Thunderhead Shard
materials.desc: A jagged shard of crystal formed inside a colossal thunderhead, booming softly when touched. A very-rare keystone for thunder, lightning and storm-calling magic.

materials.name: Eye-of-the-Storm Glass
materials.desc: A perfectly calm, clear sphere of glass formed in the still heart of an eternal storm; air around it goes silent. A legendary keystone for mastery of wind and storm.

materials.name: Earthheart Geode
materials.desc: A heavy, fist-sized geode that thrums like a slow heartbeat; cracked open, its violet crystals feel warm and alive. A very-rare keystone for earth, tremor and stone-shaping magic.

materials.name: Living Stone
materials.desc: Grey stone that slowly flows like cold clay between your fingers and hardens when released. Used in digging tools, stone-passing boots and earth-gliding magic.

materials.name: Deep Gem Cluster
materials.desc: A fused knot of rough garnets, beryls and spinels from Elemental Earth or the deepest Underdark caverns, still gritty with primordial dust. Jewellers split it into many small focus stones.

materials.name: Worldheart Diamond
materials.desc: A diamond the size of a heart, grown under the unimaginable weight of the Plane of Earth's core; it cannot be scratched by anything mortal. A legendary keystone for invulnerability and earth mastery.

materials.name: Brimstone
materials.desc: Yellow-black, sulphur-reeking rock that smoulders faintly and never quite cools. A staple of fiendish fire magic, summoning circles and hellish incense.

materials.name: Hellfire Ember
materials.desc: A red-black ember that burns cold at the edges and scorches the soul as much as the flesh. It dies within an hour unless sealed in iron; used for infernal weapons and fire that ignores resistance.

materials.name: Infernal Iron Ore
materials.desc: Dark red ore streaked with veins that pulse like cooling blood, mined from the slag-fields of the Hells. Forged into devilish blades that bite deeper against the righteous.

materials.name: Abyssal Thornvine
materials.desc: A black, barbed vine that twitches toward warm bodies and whispers when cut. Chaotic, madness-inducing magic and cruel binding cords.

materials.name: Water of the Styx
materials.desc: Oily black water that sucks memories out of anyone it touches; even the fumes blur the mind. A very-rare keystone for forgetfulness, mind-wiping and powerful curses.

materials.name: Hellfield Ash
materials.desc: Grey-red ash from the eternal battlefields of the first Hell, still faintly warm and smelling of blood. Cheap infernal reagent and fire-ink pigment.

materials.name: Celestial Dew
materials.desc: Dew from the meadows of the Upper Planes that glows with soft golden light and tastes of honey. A rare keystone for holy healing and restoration potions.

materials.name: Celestia Sun-Amber
materials.desc: Amber from the slopes of the seven-tiered mountain, with a speck of living sunlight trapped inside. Radiant weapons, sun blades and wards against undead.

materials.name: Holy Spring Water
materials.desc: Crystal-clear water from a sanctified spring, so pure it glows faintly in shadow; the strongest wells rise on the Upper Planes. Stronger than temple holy water; blessing and consecration magic.

materials.name: Halo Quartz
materials.desc: Clear quartz ringed by a floating band of pale light. Holy symbols, protective amulets and light magic.

materials.name: Manna
materials.desc: Sweet, flaky white bread that settles like dew at dawn on hallowed ground, most abundantly on the Upper Planes. One mouthful sustains a traveller for a day.

materials.name: Celestial Lifesap
materials.desc: Golden sap that wells from the bark of a tree of life on the Upper Planes; a single drop heals any wound. A legendary keystone for resurrection and eternal youth.

materials.name: Astral Silver Thread
materials.desc: A strand of silvery light, cool and weightless, severed from a long-abandoned astral tether. Woven into planar travel magic and teleport-binding tapestries.

materials.name: Thought Crystal
materials.desc: Translucent crystal grown from the thoughts of astral travellers; hold it and you hear distant voices. Telepathy and mind-reading magic.

materials.name: Drifting Ioun Shard
materials.desc: A faceted crystal shard that insists on orbiting your head when released. The raw stuff of Ioun stones and other arcane and knowledge magic.

materials.name: Mind-Mote Dust
materials.desc: Glittering silver dust that condenses from stray thoughts, thickest in the Astral Sea; it tastes like forgotten memories. Divination and memory inks.

materials.name: Colour-Pool Glass
materials.desc: Iridescent glass that condenses on the rim of an astral colour pool, cycling through hues. Used for portal keys and teleportation magic.

materials.name: Dead God Stone
materials.desc: A stone flake from the petrified corpse of a forgotten god drifting in the Astral Sea; it holds a fading echo of divinity. A legendary keystone for artifacts and divine magic.

environments.name: Arctic & Tundra
environments.desc: Endless white under a low sun, where life clings to rock and ice in hardy lichens and berries. Blizzards, thin ice and white-furred predators claim the careless forager.
environments.forage: Short summer window for plants; in deep winter only ice, minerals and lichens can be gathered, and every hour outside risks exhaustion from cold.

gather.cond: Scraped from wind-scoured rocks; brittle — cut it with a warm blade or it shatters to worthless powder.
gather.riskWhy: Bare, wind-scoured rock: nowhere to hide if a wolf pack crests the rise.

gather.cond: Only in the brief summer thaw; hidden under the first light snow in autumn.
gather.riskWhy: Bears fattening for winter strip the same bushes in the thaw.

gather.cond: Grows from cracks in glacier faces; reaching it requires a DC 13 Athletics check or a fall into a crevasse.
gather.riskWhy: Glacier faces are mephit haunts, and wyrmlings den in the crevasses below.

gather.cond: Hewn from old glacier cores; carry it wrapped in fur or it thaws in a day.
gather.riskWhy: Old glacier cores draw ice mephits, and bears pad the ice edge.

gather.cond: Forms on ridgelines only during a hard blizzard; each hour searching demands a DC 12 Con save vs exhaustion.

guard.note: A winter wolf pack hunts the ridgelines in the same blizzards that raise the crystals.

gather.riskWhy: Blizzard ridgelines are winter wolf hunting grounds; you are blind and they are not.

gather.cond: Only on nights when the aurora touches the ground; the glass is gone by dawn. Gather it barehanded and take 1d6 cold damage.

guard.note: An adult white dragon basks on the glowing snowfields on aurora nights and hoards the glass it finds.

gather.riskWhy: The glowing snowfield is a dragon's basking ground, and the glass is its hoard.

gather.cond: Dark lumps easily spotted against the snow on ancient impact fields; DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) to find the first.

guard.note: A remorhaz hunts beneath the impact field, drawn up through the snow by the warmth of anyone digging.

gather.riskWhy: Digging warms the snow, and warmth calls up what burrows beneath the impact field.

gather.cond: Only within a frozen rift where the Plane of Water bleeds through; the rift's chill deals 2d6 cold damage per hour.

guard.note: An ice devil stands sentry at the rift, sent by its masters to claim the ice before mortals do.

gather.riskWhy: A planar rift with a devil at the gate; elementals seep through with the cold.

gather.cond: Rarely exposed in frost-shattered scree below high ice cliffs; one find per week of searching at most.

guard.note: Frost giants work the same scree for jewels to trade, and they break the legs of rival prospectors.

gather.riskWhy: Frost giant prospectors work this scree and do not share it.

gather.cond: From windswept salt flats exposed by summer melt.
gather.riskWhy: Elk come to lick the flats, and the wolves come for the elk.

gather.cond: Low, woolly tufts sheltering in rock hollows on the tundra; summer only.
gather.riskWhy: Sheltered hollows on the open tundra; foxes, wolves and the odd bear pass through.

gather.cond: Carpets the southern tundra edge in summer.
gather.riskWhy: The mild southern edge of the tundra; herders graze here all summer.

gather.cond: Rusty outcrops exposed by retreating glaciers.
gather.riskWhy: Fresh glacier scars: loose ice, a stray mephit, a curious bear.

gather.cond: In salt caves under the permafrost; glows under moonlight, making night the best time to find it.
gather.riskWhy: Salt caves under the permafrost, searched by night: something always shelters inside.

gather.cond: From dwarf birches on the southern tundra edge.
gather.riskWhy: Dwarf birch at the tundra's edge, a short walk from camp.

gather.cond: Shaken loose from frost-shattered granite in the high tundra.
gather.riskWhy: Frost-shattered granite on the high tundra, where big cats and wolves roam.

gather.cond: In ice caves where the sun reaches through clear ice; it splits the light into rainbows at noon.

guard.note: A white dragon wyrmling dens in the ice caves and snaps at anything that blocks its light.

gather.riskWhy: The ice caves are a wyrmling's den, and you are standing in its sunlight.

environments.name: Coasts & Shorelines
environments.desc: Tidal flats, sea cliffs and wrack-strewn beaches where the ocean leaves its treasures twice a day. Rogue waves, crumbling cliffs and territorial sea-birds make the work lively.
environments.forage: Best at low tide, and best of all after a storm has churned the sea; many finds are washed away by the next high tide.

gather.cond: Raked from sunny tidal pans; easy in dry weather, impossible in rain.
gather.riskWhy: Sunny tidal pans by the shore road; the crabs are the only locals.

gather.cond: Piled along the strand line after every tide.
gather.riskWhy: Heaped on the strand line for anyone to rake up.

gather.cond: In sheltered rock pools at low tide.
gather.riskWhy: Rock pools hide pinching crabs and the occasional grasping octopus.

gather.cond: On muddy salt marsh edges in late summer.
gather.riskWhy: Soft salt-marsh mud where crocodiles and snakes bask in warm climes.

gather.cond: Along the strand after onshore winds.
gather.riskWhy: A quiet strand; harpies and beachcombing bears are the worst of it.

gather.cond: In shingle near old harbour towns.
gather.riskWhy: Shingle beside the old harbour, in sight of the town walls.

gather.cond: In warm shallows; a DC 10 Athletics check to dive for it.
gather.riskWhy: Warm shallows are a reef shark's hunting ground, if a quiet one.

gather.cond: On the outer edge of warm reefs at the lowest spring tides; sharp coral cuts deal 1d4 slashing damage.
gather.riskWhy: The reef's outer edge, with coral cuts in the water: sharks and merrow come to the blood.

gather.cond: Pry open oysters on submerged beds; DC 12 Con save each dive or gain a level of exhaustion.
gather.riskWhy: Dive after dive over the oyster beds; octopuses lurk and merrow covet pearls.

gather.cond: Only after a winter storm, and only on shores where whales pass; DC 15 Perception to spot it among the wrack.
gather.riskWhy: Storm-wrack on whale shores draws scavengers and the odd bear.

gather.cond: From warm coast mangrove swamps.
gather.riskWhy: Mangrove roots are crocodile and constrictor country.

gather.cond: On sun-baked, sandy coastal hills.
gather.riskWhy: Sun-baked dune hills behind the beach; nothing hunts there at noon.

gather.cond: Only on beaches beside volcanic islands.
gather.riskWhy: Volcanic beaches steam with mephits and host pteranodon roosts.

gather.cond: Washed ashore after deep-sea storms in the far south; empty shells only.
gather.riskWhy: Storm-washed southern strands; merrow sometimes follow the flotsam in.

gather.cond: Rarely found in sea-cliff pegmatite veins; climbing to them requires a DC 13 Athletics check.
gather.riskWhy: Clinging to a sea cliff among harpy and pteranodon nests.

gather.cond: From white chalk cliffs; beware falling rock (DC 12 Dex save or 2d6 bludgeoning).
gather.riskWhy: Cliff-foot work under roosting seabirds and the odd harpy.

gather.cond: Nodules weathered out of chalk cliffs.
gather.riskWhy: Nodules picked off the beach below the cliffs.

gather.cond: Washes ashore on cold northern beaches after autumn storms; look for it in the tangled seaweed.
gather.riskWhy: Cold northern beaches after a storm; bears and crabs pick over the same wrack.

gather.cond: Blue clay exposed at the foot of eroding cliffs.
gather.riskWhy: Dug at the cliff foot near the fishing villages.

gather.cond: Sieved from the finest dunes.
gather.riskWhy: Sieved from open dunes in plain sight of the shore path.

gather.cond: Scraped from sun-dried salt pans above the tide line.
gather.riskWhy: Salt pans above the tide line, worked by villagers every summer.

environments.name: Deserts & Badlands
environments.desc: Dune seas, salt pans and wind-carved canyons that bake by day and freeze by night. What grows here is tough, bitter and often poisonous; what lies here was often buried for a reason.
environments.forage: Forage at dawn and dusk; searching at midday requires a DC 12 Con save each hour vs heat exhaustion. Water is scarcer than any reagent.

gather.cond: Only on dune crests that caught the full noon sun; scoop it at dusk while it still glows. It burns bare skin (1d4 fire).
gather.riskWhy: Dune crests at dusk, the very hour the desert's hunters wake.

gather.cond: Found only in the days after a desert thunderstorm; dig carefully — the glass tube shatters on a failed check.

guard.note: A blue dragon wyrmling chases the thunderstorms and digs up fulgurite for its hoard.

gather.riskWhy: A blue wyrmling chases the same storms and does not share its glass.

gather.cond: Dug from the crust of dry salt pans.
gather.riskWhy: Open salt pans; lizards and dust mephits drift across the crust.

gather.cond: From the edges of dry soda lakes.
gather.riskWhy: Soda lake shores: dust devils, hyenas and the jackals of the embalmers' trade.

gather.cond: Anywhere; the purest comes from white dunes.
gather.riskWhy: Scooped from any dune near the caravan road.

gather.cond: Tapped from twisted desert trees in the rocky wadis; the resin weeps only in the hottest month.
gather.riskWhy: Rocky wadis in the hottest month, when snakes shelter under every stone.

gather.cond: Thorny shrubs in rocky desert borders; the thorns carry a mild poison (DC 10 Con save or poisoned 1 hour).
gather.riskWhy: Thorny scrub at the desert border hides snakes and wolf spiders.

gather.cond: Tapped from umbrella-shaped dragon trees on high desert plateaus; one tree yields once a season.

guard.note: A manticore nests among the dragon trees and shoots tail-spikes at tappers.

gather.riskWhy: The dragon trees are a manticore's roost, and tappers are easy targets.

gather.cond: Common in oases and rocky slopes.
gather.riskWhy: Grows around the oases where caravans water.

gather.cond: Only in oases that appear on no map; DC 15 Wisdom save or you wander after false blooms and lose a day.

guard.note: A gynosphinx keeps the unmapped oasis and lets pass only those who solve her riddle.

gather.riskWhy: An unmapped oasis kept by a riddling sphinx; illusions lure the unwary to worse.

gather.cond: In copper-stained canyon walls; flash floods can fill the canyons in minutes during the rainy season.
gather.riskWhy: Narrow canyons: snakes in the cracks and a manticore on the rim.

gather.cond: In granite outcrops after flash floods expose new faces.
gather.riskWhy: Fresh granite faces after a flood; lions and scorpions shelter in the rocks.

gather.cond: Glitters in wind-scoured basalt at sunrise; invisible at any other time.
gather.riskWhy: Basalt at sunrise, when the lizards come out to warm themselves.

gather.cond: Green-streaked canyon walls.
gather.riskWhy: Canyon walls with the usual snakes and lizards in the shade.

gather.cond: Placer flakes in dry washes; requires water to pan.
gather.riskWhy: Panning dry washes; a brass wyrmling can smell gold from a mile off.

gather.cond: Scraped from the walls of desert caves.
gather.riskWhy: Desert caves are dens for scorpions, spiders and beetle swarms.

gather.cond: Only around the ruins of a fallen desert kingdom; it blooms at midnight. Handling it barehanded forces a DC 15 Con save vs poison.

guard.note: A spirit naga, once the fallen kingdom's court poisoner, still coils among the ruined midnight gardens.

gather.riskWhy: Midnight in a dead kingdom's garden, where its poisoner and its dead still keep court.

gather.cond: In the crusts around hot springs in the badlands; the fumes are toxic (DC 12 Con save or poisoned 1 hour).
gather.riskWhy: Badland hot springs fizz with mephits; lizards bask on the warm crust.

gather.cond: In the sun-baked clay of desert badlands where an ancient sea dried away; crack the nodules open to find the colour.
gather.riskWhy: Cracking nodules in open badlands; hyenas and scorpions keep watch.

gather.cond: Falls with the dew around a desert hermitage sanctified by an old saint; it melts by mid-morning, so gather it at first light.
gather.riskWhy: Gathered at dawn outside a saint's hermitage; the holy ground keeps beasts off.

gather.cond: Wind-sorted white sand from the deep dunes.
gather.riskWhy: The deep dunes are far from water and full of burrowers.

gather.cond: Crusts on the floor of dry salt lakes.
gather.riskWhy: Salt-lake crust worked by caravaneers year-round.

environments.name: Forests & Woodlands
environments.desc: Ancient oak, dim pine and bright birch woods, the richest foraging ground in the mortal world. Wolves, owlbears, territorial druids and worse haunt the deep groves.
environments.forage: Easy and plentiful from spring to autumn; halve yields in winter, when only bark, wood, fungi and mosses remain.

gather.cond: On the north side of old trees and stones; best after rain.
gather.riskWhy: Ordinary woodland work; a boar or a bear might amble past.

gather.cond: In sunlit clearings; the silver undersides give it away on a breezy day.
gather.riskWhy: Sunlit clearings where boars root and wasps drone.

gather.cond: Only in old-growth groves touched by the Feywild; best gathered at dusk, when the leaves stop hiding.

guard.note: A green hag harvests the same vines for her own glamours and treats the grove as her garden.

gather.riskWhy: This is a green hag's garden, and she is gathering the same vines.

gather.cond: Along cold streams under ancient trees; the gel spoils if the leaf is crushed.
gather.riskWhy: Cold streams under ancient trees: troll country, and trolls love this leaf.

gather.cond: Old yews in churchyards and deep forest; cut in winter when the sap is low.
gather.riskWhy: Winter yews, lonely churchyards: hungry wolves, and wisps among the graves.

gather.cond: Rare trees in the deepest forest; felling one takes a day and dulls three axes.

guard.note: An owlbear dens in the hollow of an ironwood, and felling one is loud work.

gather.riskWhy: An owlbear dens in the hollow trunk, and a day of chopping wakes it.

gather.cond: Only from an oak at least a thousand years old that has fallen naturally — cutting a living one draws the wrath of the forest's guardians.

guard.note: A treant tends the fallen oak as it would a dying elder and judges every axe brought near it.

gather.riskWhy: A treant's dying elder; every axe is judged by the forest itself.

gather.cond: Where the Feywild bleeds through; only branches shed willingly under a full moon hold their magic.

guard.note: A green hag lives where the veil is thin and demands a price for every branch.

gather.riskWhy: The veil is thin, a hag sets the price, and fey mischief rides the full moon.

gather.cond: Smothering old walls and tree trunks.
gather.riskWhy: Grows on any old wall or trunk near the path.

gather.cond: Under beech and oak in autumn; handle with gloves or make a DC 12 Con save vs poison.
gather.riskWhy: Deep leaf litter under old oaks: boars root here, centipedes and spiders lurk.

gather.cond: On oak twigs in autumn.
gather.riskWhy: Picked off oak twigs at the wood's edge.

gather.cond: Weeping from scarred pines.
gather.riskWhy: Tapped from the pines at the forest edge; nothing bothers a resin-gatherer.

gather.cond: From wild hives in hollow trees; DC 12 Survival to smoke out the bees, or take 2d4 piercing from stings.
gather.riskWhy: Wild hives: angry bees, and the bears that raid them.

gather.cond: Anywhere trees grow; felling takes an hour per load.
gather.riskWhy: An hour of loud chopping tells the whole wood where you are.

gather.cond: Thick on the floor of deep, windless hollows; walk on it and even birds fall silent.
gather.riskWhy: Silent hollows where birds fall quiet because something is hunting.

gather.cond: From rare charcoal-barked trees in the gloomiest stands; fell it at night, when its grain is loosest, or it splinters.

guard.note: Ettercaps web the gloomiest stands and wait for night-time woodcutters.

gather.riskWhy: Ettercap webs fill the gloomiest stands, and you must come at night.

gather.cond: Pried in plates from ancient trees; takes an hour and a crowbar per plate.
gather.riskWhy: An hour of prying at an ancient trunk, deep in owlbear and bear country.

gather.cond: Tapped from golden-barked pines in spring; it glues your fingers together if you are careless.
gather.riskWhy: Sticky fingers and sweet sap draw wasps, and sometimes a bear.

gather.cond: Sprouts in the grey ash of a burned-over wood in the first weeks after the fire; gone once the green returns.
gather.riskWhy: The burned wood is open ground; fire beetles and scavengers pick through the ash.

gather.cond: From silver birches in moonlit glades far from any road; strip no more than a hand's width per tree or it sickens.
gather.riskWhy: Moonlit glades far from roads: werewolves hate the silver, wisps love the dark.

gather.cond: Common wayside herbs: comfrey, plantain, self-heal. Easy to find along any path.
gather.riskWhy: Wayside herbs along any path; nothing but passing travellers.

gather.cond: Foxglove, lords-and-ladies and yew berries in shaded clearings. Gloves advised.
gather.riskWhy: Shaded clearings where snakes coil among the foxglove.

gather.cond: Honeysuckle and violets at the woodland edge.
gather.riskWhy: The sunny woodland edge, busy with nothing worse than bees.

gather.cond: A seasoned, straight-grained bough from an old tree. An hour with an axe and a saw.
gather.riskWhy: Felling an old bough is noisy work in an ordinary wood.

environments.name: Grasslands & Plains
environments.desc: Rolling prairies, flower meadows and farmland stretching to the horizon. Open ground means few places to hide from stampeding herds, raiders or a summer storm.
environments.forage: Best in spring and summer when flowers bloom; after harvest and in winter, only roots and seeds remain.

gather.cond: Along meadow streams.
gather.riskWhy: Meadow streams where boars wallow and cockatrices hunt frogs.

gather.cond: Everywhere in summer; grazing herds avoid it.
gather.riskWhy: Grows everywhere, even in the pastures by the farmhouse.

gather.cond: In field margins in early summer; picking many at once forces a DC 10 Con save or you fall asleep for 10 minutes.
gather.riskWhy: Nod off in the field margin and the wolves or spiders will find you first.

gather.cond: Dry, sunny field edges.
gather.riskWhy: Sunny field edges within sight of the farm.

gather.cond: One per full day of searching; roll a d20 — only on a 15+ do you find it.
gather.riskWhy: A long day on your knees in open meadow; something always wanders by.

gather.cond: Only on the windiest days of late summer; chase the puffs as they rise — a DC 13 Acrobatics check to catch a handful.
gather.riskWhy: Chasing puffs across the plain, eyes up, straight into griffon and hippogriff skies.

gather.cond: Grows alone on hilltops overlooking battlefields; best picked at noon.
gather.riskWhy: Lone hilltops over old battlefields: lions keep watch, and the fallen ride again.

gather.cond: Opens only in the hour after a thunderstorm; touching it deals 1 lightning damage.
gather.riskWhy: Open plain after a storm, when ankhegs surface in the soaked soil.

gather.cond: On thorny hedgerows in autumn; the bushes twitch and scratch (1 slashing damage).
gather.riskWhy: The hedge twitches because some of it is awake, and wasps nest in the thorns.

gather.cond: Dug from rich, dark soil in autumn.
gather.riskWhy: Digging rich soil where ankhegs and bulettes feel every spade.

gather.cond: Around farmsteads and roadsides.
gather.riskWhy: Roadside and farmstead weeds; the farm dog is the only threat.

gather.cond: Wild flax in late summer.
gather.riskWhy: Wild flax in the open field; carters pass all day.

gather.cond: In wet meadows in summer.
gather.riskWhy: Wet meadows: biting swarms, adders and the odd boar in the reeds.

gather.cond: Hedgerows in late summer and autumn.
gather.riskWhy: Roadside hedgerows; you may share them with a boar.

gather.cond: Shrubs along warm, southern plains.
gather.riskWhy: Warm southern plains are big-cat and hyena country.

gather.cond: Wild roses that bloom only on midsummer's eve; each bush yields one magical bloom.
gather.riskWhy: Midsummer's eve in the wild roses; shapechangers love a festival night.

gather.cond: From elder bushes in hedgerows; folk say to ask the Elder Mother's permission before cutting.
gather.riskWhy: Cut without asking and the Elder Mother's servants answer.

gather.cond: From dense blackthorn hedges in winter, when the thorns are hardest; 1d4 piercing from the thorns.
gather.riskWhy: Thick winter hedges shelter hungry wolves and worse.

gather.cond: Meadow herbs picked along field margins and hedgerows.
gather.riskWhy: Field margins and hedgerows in farm country.

gather.cond: Wild roses, meadowsweet and lavender in high summer.
gather.riskWhy: High-summer meadows humming with bees and nothing worse.

gather.cond: Wild hemp along field edges, retted in a pond for a week to free the fibre.
gather.riskWhy: Wild hemp at the field edge, retted in the farm pond.

environments.name: Hills & Highlands
environments.desc: Heather moors, barrow-studded downs and rocky tors where the wind never stops. Old cairns, giants' stones and ore seams make the highlands a prospector's delight.
environments.forage: Moderate all year; fog can roll in within minutes, and the barrows are best left undisturbed after dark.

gather.cond: Covers the moors; best in late summer.
gather.riskWhy: Open moorland in plain view; only sheep and the odd hawk for company.

gather.cond: In sheltered valley soils.
gather.riskWhy: Sheltered valleys draw boar and badgers rooting for the same tubers.

gather.cond: Beneath standing stones and giant-built cairns; digging it out takes an hour and a DC 13 Athletics check.

guard.note: An ettin sleeps in the cairn-ring and both its heads wake to the sound of digging.

gather.riskWhy: Digging in a giant's cairn-ring; the sleeper's kin and hill ogres roam nearby.

gather.cond: On damp north-facing rocks.
gather.riskWhy: Quiet north faces; a wolf or a startled snake is the usual trouble.

gather.cond: From lone trees on hilltops struck in a recent storm; the charge fades after a month.
gather.riskWhy: Lone hilltop trees are exposed perches for griffons and hippogriffs hunting below.

gather.cond: Along highland streams.
gather.riskWhy: Streamside willows below the farms; deer drink here, little else.

gather.cond: Glinting in the scree below schist outcrops after rain washes the dust away.
gather.riskWhy: Scree below the outcrops; lizards bask and snakes shelter in the rubble.

gather.cond: Washed out of shale banks in highland stream beds by spring floods; the lighter the piece, the better.
gather.riskWhy: Highland stream beds, walked by deer and the wolves that follow them.

gather.cond: Only in streams below old battlefields; best found after heavy rain.
gather.riskWhy: Old battlefield streams; the restless fallen and scavengers linger nearby.

gather.cond: In geodes cracked from hillside basalt; you must break a dozen to find one worth keeping.
gather.riskWhy: Hammering geodes on open hillsides carries far; curious beasts come to look.

gather.cond: Lying in dry stream beds; tap each one to hear if it whispers.
gather.riskWhy: Tapping stones in dry beds; the whispers draw hyenas and worse.

gather.cond: Rust-red outcrops; easy digging.
gather.riskWhy: Surface outcrops near the drover roads; easy, open work.

gather.cond: Green-stained hillside seams.
gather.riskWhy: Open seams on quiet slopes; a young copper dragon may come sniffing for metal.

gather.cond: Deep in old mine workings; DC 12 Con save vs bad air each hour below.
gather.riskWhy: Abandoned mine workings: bats, stirges and whatever moved into the dark.

gather.cond: Surface seams in valley sides.
gather.riskWhy: Surface seams by the valley farms; the worst you'll meet is a sheepdog.

gather.cond: Under gallows-trees on lonely hills; its scream when pulled forces a DC 13 Wisdom save or be frightened for 1 minute.

guard.note: The wight of a man hanged on the gallows-tree rises when the mandrake screams.

gather.riskWhy: A gallows-hill at night, and the scream wakes the hanged dead.

gather.cond: In damp hollows and ditches; gloves required.
gather.riskWhy: Ditches and damp hollows; snakes shelter in the wet grass.

gather.cond: On damp, shaded slopes near wolf country; plucking it barehanded forces a DC 10 Con save vs poison.
gather.riskWhy: It grows where the wolves den, and some of those wolves walk on two legs.

gather.cond: In the milky quartz veins of hillside quarries and streambeds; the pink pieces are a small share of the whole.
gather.riskWhy: Quarry faces and streambeds; hill goats and the odd panther keep watch.

gather.cond: Green crusts in the weathered tops of copper deposits; the dust is toxic in closed tunnels (DC 11 Con save).
gather.riskWhy: Weathered copper caps on open ground; burrowers sometimes break the surface.

gather.cond: Cut from an open marble quarry on the hillside; a day's work with wedges and a sledge, and the blocks are heavy to move.
gather.riskWhy: A day's hammering in an open quarry; the noise draws ogres looking for easy meat.

gather.cond: In a grassed-over crater among the hills where a star fell long ago; the lumps lie under a foot of turf and set compasses spinning.

guard.note: A chimera has made the crater its den and burns anything that digs in it.

gather.riskWhy: Digging in a chimera's den; the crater is its hunting ground and larder.

gather.cond: From a spring beneath a hilltop shrine where a saint was buried; it keeps its blessing only if drawn with a prayer and a gift left behind.
gather.riskWhy: A tended shrine on a pilgrims' path; the saint's peace keeps predators off.

gather.cond: Thyme, sorrel and betony on sunny slopes.
gather.riskWhy: Sunny slopes near the sheep-runs; just bees and grazing ponies.

gather.cond: Pale outcrops; it breaks into blocks with a hammer and wedges.
gather.riskWhy: Pale outcrops by the tracks; no one troubles a stone-breaker here.

gather.cond: In old, half-collapsed miners' trial pits.
gather.riskWhy: Half-collapsed trial pits make snug dens for badgers and giant weasels.

environments.name: Mountains & Peaks
environments.desc: Towering crags, ice-cold tarns and thin air above the treeline. Avalanches, rockfalls and wyverns guard the richest mineral veins in the world.
environments.forage: Summer only above the snowline; each hour of searching on high slopes requires a DC 12 Athletics check or a fall. Altitude sickness plagues those who linger.

gather.cond: Growing straight through granite cracks; must be chiselled out whole.
gather.riskWhy: Hours of chiselling on bare granite; the ringing draws gargoyles and giant goats.

gather.cond: On high, north-facing crags above the snowline.
gather.riskWhy: High snow crags are winter wolf and sabre-tooth country.

gather.cond: In misty ravines where updrafts keep the fronds aloft.
gather.riskWhy: Misty ravines where eagles ride the updrafts, and harpies sing.

gather.cond: Only in a single hidden tarn on the highest peak, where the ice never melts; guardians and a DC 16 Con save vs altitude await.

guard.note: An adult silver dragon lairs above the tarn and tests the intent of every climber who reaches it.

gather.riskWhy: The highest tarn is a silver dragon's lair; it judges every climber.

gather.cond: Where compasses spin wildly; follow the needle to the source.
gather.riskWhy: Spinning compasses mark iron-rich rock where xorn and earth spirits stir.

gather.cond: In veins of white rock along the ridges; easy pickings on the lower slopes.
gather.riskWhy: Easy pickings on the lower ridges within sight of the passes.

gather.cond: Glittering flakes in granite.
gather.riskWhy: Glittering flakes in roadside granite; nothing hunts a mica-gatherer.

gather.cond: Only in rare pegmatite pockets high on the peaks; a week of searching per find.

guard.note: Stone giants consider the pegmatite pockets sacred carvings-in-waiting and hurl boulders at miners.

gather.riskWhy: A week in sacred giant pockets; stone giants hurl boulders at trespassers.

gather.cond: Only in ancient volcanic pipes; one find per season of back-breaking work.

guard.note: A fire giant clan works the old volcanic pipe as a forge-mine and keeps every stone it yields.

gather.riskWhy: A fire giant clan's forge-mine; every stone taken is theft from them.

gather.cond: In ice-cold caves that sing when the wind blows.
gather.riskWhy: Singing ice caves shelter bears and mephits; the ringing gives you away.

gather.cond: Everywhere in the lower slopes.
gather.riskWhy: Common on the lower slopes near the mining villages.

gather.cond: Deep veins under the peaks, reached by old dwarven mine-shafts; many shafts are no longer empty.
gather.riskWhy: Old dwarven shafts are no longer empty; trolls and gargoyles move in.

gather.cond: In quartz seams high on the mountains; the richest ones are held by dwarven claims or dragon hoards.
gather.riskWhy: The rich seams sit near dragon hoards; greedy wyrmlings smell the gold.

gather.cond: Only in deep veins beneath ancient dwarven holds; each hour of mining requires a DC 13 Con save vs bad air.
gather.riskWhy: Deep beneath ancient holds, where whatever emptied them still dwells.

gather.cond: Only on the windiest summit ridges; the seedhead tries to escape — a DC 15 Dexterity check to catch it.

guard.note: A roc nests on the summit ridge and treats anything climbing there as prey.

gather.riskWhy: The summit ridge is a roc's nest; anything moving there is prey.

gather.cond: Only on slopes where a dragon was slain; the ground there is still scorched, and the dragon's kin may be watching.

guard.note: A red dragon wyrmling of the slain dragon's line haunts the scorched slope.

gather.riskWhy: A dragon's death-slope; its kin and the fire beasts it bred still prowl.

gather.cond: The mountain ash grows alone on high crags; its berries ripen red in autumn, the best time to cut.
gather.riskWhy: Lone crag trees; a blood hawk nest or a hungry bear in berry season.

gather.cond: In high cloud-forests; visible only as a gap in the mist, and only while the mist lasts. DC 16 Perception to spot.

guard.note: A young silver dragon glides through the cloud-forest in the mist and guards the orchids as its garden.

gather.riskWhy: The mist garden of a young silver dragon; it glides unseen among the orchids.

gather.cond: Crusted around volcanic vents on smoking peaks; the sulphur fumes force a DC 12 Con save or poisoned for 1 hour.
gather.riskWhy: Smoking vents where magmin and hell hounds bask in the sulphur.

gather.cond: Knapped from fresh lava flows on an active volcano once the crust has cooled for a day; break through and take 4d10 fire damage.
gather.riskWhy: Walking fresh lava fields beside fire elementals and salamanders.

gather.cond: Red crusts around hot springs and old volcanic vents; heating it releases toxic fumes (DC 13 Con save or poisoned 1 hour).
gather.riskWhy: Hot springs and old vents attract mephits and the beasts that bathe there.

gather.cond: Around peaks warped by wild magic or an old planar storm, where small chunks of rock drift in the air; tether them before they float away.
gather.riskWhy: Wild-magic peaks where elementals drift through the planar cracks.

gather.cond: In blue seams high in dry mountains; old miners' trails lead to the best faces.
gather.riskWhy: Old miners' trails through dry peaks; manticores sometimes watch them.

gather.cond: Rooted in steaming cracks on the warm slopes of an active volcano; pick it only with fire-resistant gloves.
gather.riskWhy: Warm volcanic slopes where magmin and hell hounds lie in the heat.

gather.cond: Green nephrite boulders tumbled down cold mountain rivers; they look like any other stone until wetted and struck.
gather.riskWhy: Cold mountain rivers; bears fish the pools and trolls wade the fords.

gather.cond: Inside the cloudbanks that never leave the highest peaks, where the Plane of Air presses close; bundle it fast before it thins.

guard.note: An air elemental has slipped through the thin place and whirls about the summit clouds.

gather.riskWhy: An air elemental whirls in the thin place, and the storm-born follow.

gather.cond: Black glass knapped from old lava flows on the flanks of volcanoes; the edges cut deep (1 slashing damage on a failed check).
gather.riskWhy: Old, cool lava flows; a stray mephit or a basilisk sunning on the rock.

gather.cond: Crusted on the ash-flats beside a lava lake in an active crater; wet it and it explodes (2d6 fire).
gather.riskWhy: The crater's lava lake is a fire elemental's hearth and a salamander's hunt.

gather.cond: Cliff faces riddled with old caves.
gather.riskWhy: Cave-riddled cliffs; bears and bats keep the old caves.

gather.cond: Dark cassiterite pebbles in stream gravels below granite peaks. Pan for it.
gather.riskWhy: Panning stream gravels below the peaks; bears and wolves come to drink.

gather.cond: Heavy grey galena in quartz veins.
gather.riskWhy: Quartz veins on quiet slopes; a harpy or wolf pack might pass.

gather.cond: Clear quartz points in cracks and geodes high on the slopes.
gather.riskWhy: High slopes above the treeline; wyverns and griffons hunt the open scree.

environments.name: Swamps & Marshes
environments.desc: Sucking bogs, stagnant pools and mangrove tangles under a haze of midges. Many of the world's deadliest poisons grow here, alongside hags, crocodiles and disease.
environments.forage: Year-round, but every day spent foraging requires a DC 11 Con save vs swamp fever; gloves and a pole are essential.

gather.cond: On damp banks in late summer; its berries look like bilberries — the unwary forager's bane.
gather.riskWhy: Damp banks with snakes in the reeds; the berries are the real killer.

gather.cond: On rotting logs in the deepest bog; the spores numb bare hands (DC 12 Con save or poisoned 1 hour).
gather.riskWhy: The deepest bog, where crocodiles lurk and spider-kin weave.

gather.cond: Common along ditch edges.
gather.riskWhy: Common ditch-weed by the causeway; only frogs and midges here.

gather.cond: In acid bogs; tip the acid into a glass vial or take 1d4 acid damage.

guard.note: A black dragon wyrmling wallows in the acid bog and guards it as its first lair.

gather.riskWhy: The acid bog is a black wyrmling's first lair, and it defends it jealously.

gather.cond: Only in still, black pools on moonless nights; its perfume forces a DC 13 Con save or sleep for 1 hour.
gather.riskWhy: Black pools on moonless nights; wisps lure the drowsy into the water.

gather.cond: Only in the deepest, darkest swamp pools at midnight; handling it barehanded forces a DC 15 Con save vs poison.

guard.note: A hydra lairs in the black pools where the lotus floats, and it rises at any splash.

gather.riskWhy: The hydra's own pools at midnight; it rises at any splash.

gather.cond: Around carcasses and stagnant water; DC 10 Con save vs disease.
gather.riskWhy: Around carcasses: ghouls, rats and scavengers come to feed.

gather.cond: Clustered where a hag's hut once stood; locals say picking them draws her attention.

guard.note: The hag who once lived here is not gone, only moved a little deeper into the bog.

gather.riskWhy: Picking them calls the hag, who has only moved a little deeper.

gather.cond: Only on old battlefields sunk into the bog, where the water runs rusty red; skeletons lie beneath.

guard.note: The drowned dead of the old battle include an ogre, and it still stands guard.

gather.riskWhy: A sunken battlefield; the drowned dead still hold the line.

gather.cond: Along the reedy margins.
gather.riskWhy: Reedy margins; a crocodile may lie in the shallows.

gather.cond: Reed beds everywhere.
gather.riskWhy: Wading reed beds with leeches, snakes and the odd hungry croc.

gather.cond: On the drier hummocks.
gather.riskWhy: Dry hummocks near the village causeways; midges are the only foe.

gather.cond: Dug from deep peat; it takes a day and a DC 13 Athletics check to haul out.
gather.riskWhy: A day of digging deep peat makes noise and smell that carry across the bog.

gather.cond: At the edges of fog banks at dawn; squeezing one blinds you briefly in its fog.
gather.riskWhy: Fog-bank edges at dawn, where wisps flicker at the margin.

gather.cond: Bog-iron nodules from red-stained peat.
gather.riskWhy: Digging red peat; stirges and snakes stir from the sodden ground.

gather.cond: Along muddy trails where animals fall and are eaten.
gather.riskWhy: It grows on the very trails where predators ambush their prey.

gather.cond: On dead trees in the drowned forest; it regrows overnight, so the same tree can be harvested daily.
gather.riskWhy: The drowned forest is dim and flooded; snakes and mounds hide among the dead trees.

gather.cond: Tapped from red-barked bloodwood trees in warm swamps; the sap flows only in the heat of midday.
gather.riskWhy: Warm swamp groves; the sap's scent draws stirges and hunting cats.

gather.cond: Hemlock water-dropwort, foxglove and marsh nightshade. Wear gloves: fail by 5 and make a DC 10 Con save or be poisoned for 1 hour.
gather.riskWhy: Common marsh plants; snakes and toads share the damp ground.

gather.cond: Dug from riverbanks and marsh edges.
gather.riskWhy: Dug from the banks by the village landing; nothing stirs but frogs.

environments.name: The Underdark
environments.desc: A lightless labyrinth of caverns, fungal forests and underground seas miles below the surface. Duergar patrols, driders and things with no names haunt its tunnels, but its minerals are unmatched.
environments.forage: No seasons; darkvision or light is required. Light attracts predators — every hour of foraging with a light source adds a chance of a wandering encounter.

gather.cond: Carpets fungal forests; easy to spot in the dark.
gather.riskWhy: Glowing fungal forests where rats and beetles graze; shriekers may wail.

gather.cond: In dry crevices high on cavern walls; easiest to spot by the faint gleam of its cap in darkvision.
gather.riskWhy: Climbing high walls where darkmantles hang and spiders spin.

gather.cond: Under the fungal forest floor; follow the smell.
gather.riskWhy: Rooting the fungal floor alongside grazing beasts and their stalkers.

gather.cond: Seeps from limestone walls; scrape it into a vial before it dries.
gather.riskWhy: Limestone seeps near the upper caves; oozes favour the damp.

gather.cond: High on cavern walls and ceilings; reaching it requires a DC 13 Athletics check.

guard.note: Gricks lie coiled in the moss on the cavern ceiling, waiting for climbers.

gather.riskWhy: Climbing into a ceiling where gricks lie coiled and waiting.

gather.cond: In damp, dead-end tunnels; its spores numb bare hands (DC 12 Con save or poisoned 1 hour).
gather.riskWhy: Dead-end tunnels are where oozes pool and cubes clean up.

gather.cond: In caverns where aberrations dwell; it whispers to you as you pick it (DC 12 Wis save or confused 1 minute).

guard.note: A gibbering mouther oozes through the fungal caverns, adding its babble to the caps' whispers.

gather.riskWhy: Aberration caverns; a gibbering mouther babbles among the caps.

gather.cond: Only where wild magic seeps from the rock; spells cast there may go awry.
gather.riskWhy: Wild-magic seeps draw arcane scavengers and things slipping between spaces.

gather.cond: Clustered in deep grottoes; the light draws cave fishers to the ceilings above.
gather.riskWhy: Deep grottoes whose light draws ceiling ambushers and swarming bats.

gather.cond: In singing caverns; strike it only once — the echo draws hunters.

guard.note: A roper stands among the crystal stalagmites, drawn by the echoes.

gather.riskWhy: The echo summons hunters; a roper already waits among the stalagmites.

gather.cond: Only in caverns where no light has ever shone; any light source makes it crumble.

guard.note: Cloakers roost in the lightless caverns and strike at anyone fumbling blind among the crystals.

gather.riskWhy: Fumbling blind in a cloaker roost; shadows drift through the black.

gather.cond: Grows around ancient anti-magic fields; spells fail within 10 feet of the bramble.

guard.note: A behir dens in the dead-magic caverns, where the spellcasters who might hunt it are helpless.

gather.riskWhy: A behir's den in dead-magic caverns; your spells won't save you.

gather.cond: In deep black-and-white veins near drow shrines; patrols guard the best seams, and chisel noise carries far.

guard.note: A drider stalks the drow shrine seams, cast out but still loyal to the stone.

gather.riskWhy: Chiselling near drow shrines under the eye of an outcast drider and its spiders.

gather.cond: Where metal things tug toward the walls; follow a hanging needle, but beware — rust monsters are drawn to the same spots.
gather.riskWhy: Iron-tugging walls are rust monster feeding grounds.

gather.cond: Scraped from cave walls near bat roosts.
gather.riskWhy: Near bat roosts; the swarms stir when you scrape below.

gather.cond: Deep veins far below the surface; each hour of mining requires a DC 13 Con save vs bad air.
gather.riskWhy: Far below the surface, where duergar-dug tunnels meet purple worm burrows.

gather.cond: Only in deep veins near ancient meteorite falls; picks break on a failed check.
gather.riskWhy: Deep meteorite veins; xorn feed on them and bigger things tunnel through.

gather.cond: In narrow side-tunnels; step on one and it shrieks, alerting everything within a mile.
gather.riskWhy: Step wrong and everything within a mile hears the shriek.

gather.cond: In geode pockets in the deepest caverns, where the rock was once pressed against Elemental Earth; the gem-glow draws hungry xorn.
gather.riskWhy: The gem-glow draws hungry xorn, and elemental earth still stirs here.

gather.cond: Settled like glittering pollen in the dead caverns where a psychic overmind once ruled; breathing it stirs up stray memories (DC 12 Wis save or stunned 1 round).
gather.riskWhy: Dead overmind caverns; aberrant leftovers and mind-twisted undead linger.
